Definition: from G1722 and a derivative of G2759; to prick in, i.e. ingraft:--graff in(-to).
BiblicalUsage: To graft in — the gardener's word. Wild olive branches are grafted into the good olive tree in Romans 11:17, and Paul says the natural branches can be grafted in again if they do not abide in unbelief in Romans 11:23. The grafting was contrary to nature in Romans 11:24, which is exactly the point: God's grace does what nature never would.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe I am a wild branch grafted into a tree I did not plant, living off a root I did not grow. I hold that grafting is grace from first to last — God cut me out of the wild and joined me to His people, and He can graft the natural branches back in again whenever they believe.
